reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a public company headquartered in Seattle, WA, founded in 1994, traded on public markets under the ticker AMZN, and recorded revenue of $716,924,000,000 for the period ending 2025-12-31. The company's website for this profile centers on Amazon SageMaker, which AWS describes as "the center for all your data, analytics, and AI," positioning it as an integrated environment for machine learning, generative AI, data processing, and SQL analytics. The platform brings together tools including SageMaker Unified Studio, HyperPod, JumpStart, MLOps capabilities, and Amazon Q Developer, an AI assistant for software development, all accessible within a single development environment.

AWS tracks two AI products on this site. Amazon SageMaker covers the full ML lifecycle, including model monitoring, bias detection, and explainability tools, and supports training, customizing, and deploying ML and foundation models on managed infrastructure. AWS Bedrock is a managed foundation model API service with IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and AgentCore for agent orchestration. SageMaker also incorporates a lakehouse architecture unifying Amazon S3 data lakes and Amazon Redshift data warehouses, with Apache Iceberg compatibility, federated query capabilities, fine-grained access controls via Amazon SageMaker Catalog, and governance features including toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking.

The held facts note 60 law exposure records associated with Washington state but list no specific litigation cases. AWS carries a verified SEC filing under CIK 0001018724, consistent with its status as a public company.
